title: Hem Singh v. State of U.P.
coram: Pankaj Mithal, J. and Pankaj Bhatia, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; cl. 6.14 installments granted; recovery stayed on payment
headnote: A consumer who did not contest electricity dues on merits, but sought time to pay, obtained a clause 6.14 installment schedule: part-deposit within one month, four later installments of the balance, recovery stayed while payments were kept, and automatic vacation of stay on default.
facts: Hem Singh approached the Allahabad High Court against a recovery certificate dated 2 August 2018 seeking to recover Rs 1,70,813 plus miscellaneous expenses from him as electricity dues. He did not challenge the demand on merits. His counsel submitted that he was ready and willing to pay if granted an installment facility. The Court recorded that section 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides for that facility.

holding_units.topic: installment facility for recovery of electricity dues
holding_units.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides an installment facility for electricity dues. The writ against a recovery certificate for Rs 1,70,813 plus miscellaneous expenses is disposed of by directing the consumer to deposit Rs 50,813 within one month; on that payment, recovery of the balance remains in abeyance if Rs 1,20,000 is paid in four equal installments of Rs 30,000 by 10 February, 10 April, 10 June and 10 August 2019, the last installment to include miscellaneous charges and any further accrual. Default in any installment automatically vacates the stay and permits the respondents to recover in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: validity of the recovery certificate and the underlying electricity dues
not_decided.note: The Court proceeded on the petitioner's willingness to pay and granted a clause 6.14 installment schedule without examining the demand.
